The paper studies the scale-invariant explainable variance fraction R-squared as a causal-order pattern in synthetic ANMs.
The paper gives consistency guarantees for greedy permutation search based on sparsity and covered-arrow/polytope walks, not the GENE risk-plus-residual-dependence score.
dHSIC is a kernel embedding discrepancy and is zero exactly at joint independence under characteristic kernels; the cited work concerns joint-independence testing.
The paper introduces xHSIC/xdCov with Gaussian null limits, consistency under fixed alternatives, and local-alternative rate results; it does not formulate adaptive GENE graph confidence sets.
